Truth Paradoxes: Make sure all statements are self-contained and do not rely on external context.
Avoid contradictions that make the puzzle unsolvable or trivial.
Check that the number of statements and their logical relations remain balanced and consistent.
Constraint Satisfaction: Make sure all constraints are clearly defined and consistent across the puzzle. Avoid ambiguous or conflicting rules that could mislead solvers.
Avoid over-constraining the puzzle so that it has only one solution. Ensure there are multiple valid paths to reach the solution.
Check that the initial clues are sufficient to allow logical deduction but not so many that the puzzle becomes trivial to solve.
Graph Theory: Make sure the graph is connected to ensure non-trivial coloring challenges.
Avoid using more colors than necessary to maintain constraint difficulty.
Check that all adjacency constraints are enforced across the entire graph.
Syllogistic Logic: Make sure all statements are in standard form and use proper quantifiers. Avoid ambiguous terms or overlapping categories.
Avoid assuming additional information not directly supported by the premises. Check for valid syllogistic forms only.
Ensure the conclusion logically follows from the premises using valid conversion, obversion, or contraposition where applicable.
Knights and Knaves: Make sure statements are logically consistent with possible roles, avoid contradictions in assumptions.
Avoid creating scenarios where both truth-tellers and liars can satisfy the statements simultaneously.
Check that each character’s statement is clearly tied to their possible role and does not introduce ambiguity.
Inequality Puzzles: Make sure all constraints are clearly defined and consistent across rows and columns. Avoid ambiguous or conflicting inequalities.
Avoid creating puzzles with multiple solutions or no solution. Ensure a unique valid grid exists based on constraints.
Check that each number from 1 to size appears exactly once in every row and column. Avoid missing or repeated numbers.
Queen Placement: Make sure each queen is in a unique row and column.
Avoid placing queens on the same diagonal by checking absolute differences.
Ensure the final board has exactly n queens and no conflicts.
Weighted Grids: Make sure the total sum of row constraints matches the total sum of column constraints.
Avoid having row or column constraints that are impossible to achieve with 1s and 0s.
Check that each row and column constraint is achievable with valid combinations of 1s and 0s.
